t: Except for the purpose of determining a person’s grade, rank, and right to promotion in the Regular Army (see section 105 (b) hereof) in computing years of active Federal military service for all purposes of any person, there shall be credited active military service in the Army Nurse Corps and in the Navy Nurse Corps, active military service rendered pursuant to an appointment under the provisions of the Act of December 22, 1942 (56 Stat. 1072), and active military service rendered pursuant, to an appointment under the Act of June 23, 1944 (58 Stat. 324).

fable.w: This provision only sets a rule for crediting prior active military service in the nurse corps when computing years of federal service. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. There is no real tempting reading here; it is purely an internal personnel-computation rule.
fable.s: in computing years of active Federal military service for all purposes of any person, there shall be credited active military service in the Army Nurse Corps and in the Navy Nurse Corps

opus.w: The section only says how years of active Federal military service are counted: service in the Army and Navy Nurse Corps, and under the 1942 and 1944 appointment Acts, is credited. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. Words like "appointment" or "promotion" might look procedural, but they describe personnel service credit, not outside participation in a federal decision.
